name: crc32
description: A parallel CRC-32 generator implementing the IEEE 802.3 / Ethernet frame check sequence (FCS), sized for 10 Gigabit Ethernet.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Parallel CRC-32 generator implementing the IEEE 802.3 / Ethernet frame check sequence (FCS), sized for 10 Gigabit Ethernet. It consumes W bits per clock (default 64, the 10GbE XGMII datapath: 64 b x 156.25 MHz = 10 Gb/s) and produces the frame FCS. The CRC uses polynomial 0x04C11DB7 with reflected input/output, init 0xFFFFFFFF, and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF (check value CRC32("123456789") = 0xCBF43926). A streaming interface asserts in_valid with W bits of data; the first valid word after reset or after in_last starts a new frame and re-initializes the CRC. Arbitrary frame byte-lengths are supported: on the last word, in_bytes gives the number of valid bytes (1..W/8) occupying the low byte lanes, and out_crc / out_valid present the frame FCS one cycle after the last word.
key_decisions: Datapath width W is a parameter (default 64, multiple of 8) so the same source covers 8 / 32 / 64-bit datapaths by changing W.
The CRC update is written as a per-bit reflected loop over the W input bits that synthesis unrolls into the parallel CRC XOR tree (unrolled LFSR architecture).

The running CRC is tapped at every byte boundary so the final, possibly partial, word can fold in only its valid bytes via an in_bytes byte-count mux (an 8:1 select for W=64), supporting arbitrary frame byte-lengths.
Pure XOR logic plus a single 32-bit CRC state register: maps to LUTs and flip-flops with no DSP and no BRAM (~608 LUTs + 66 FF at W=64 on zeroasic_z1015, no latches).
The width 64 refers to the datapath, not the polynomial width; the 10GbE FCS remains CRC-32.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: W. W. Peterson and D. T. Brown, 'Cyclic codes for error detection,' Proc. IRE, vol. 49, no. 1, pp. 228-235, Jan. 1961.
IEEE Std 802.3 (Ethernet), frame check sequence: CRC-32, polynomial 0x04C11DB7, reflected, init/xorout 0xFFFFFFFF. Check value 0xCBF43926.
T.-B. Pei and C. Zukowski, 'High-speed parallel CRC circuits in VLSI,' IEEE Trans. Communications, vol. 40, no. 4, pp. 653-657, Apr. 1992.
G. Albertengo and R. Sisto, 'Parallel CRC generation,' IEEE Micro, vol. 10, no. 5, pp. 63-71, Oct. 1990.
D. V. Sarwate, 'Computation of cyclic redundancy checks via table look-up,' Communications of the ACM, vol. 31, no. 8, pp. 1008-1013, Aug. 1988.
